canonical_name: Traditional NAT / NAPT family, RFC 3022 generation

standardized.notes: Later descendant retained to clarify the family split.

roles: address-and-port translation allowing multiple local endpoints to share global addresses
addressing: Basic NAT translates addresses; NAPT additionally translates transport/identifier fields to multiplex many local endpoints through fewer global addresses.

operations.monitoring: Per-mapping/per-session translation state becomes central for NAPT.
operations.diagnostics: Port mapping, timeout and protocol-helper state affect observable reachability.
operations.failure_behavior: Loss of translation state breaks active sessions; protocols carrying embedded addresses may require special handling.
operations.operator_interface: Vendor/firewall/router implementation syntax varies and must be catalogued separately.

open_questions: Build Basic NAT versus NAPT implementation chronology by vendor.
Trace Linux/BSD and consumer-router NAT implementations.
Separate address/port translation from firewall-policy genealogy.

related_artifacts.relation: formal descendant/specification expansion of RFC 1631 NAT

notes: Do not retroactively call every RFC 1631 implementation NAPT; the later standard explicitly distinguishes the mechanisms.
